name: EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure (EdgeCore Internet Real Estate, LLC)
headquarters: Denver, Colorado, USA (999 17th Street, Suite 200); Northern Virginia office in Sterling, VA
employees: Not disclosed; 'Employee growth 145%' in 2025 and workforce 'more than doubled' since October 2023 (January 2026 release)
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure is a Denver-based single-tenant hyperscale developer owned since November 2022 by Partners Group 'on behalf of its clients' (initial commitment up to USD 1.2 billion; a further USD 1.9 billion equity round in September 2024 with Partners Group remaining majority investor), which entered 2026 claiming 'more than 1.8 gigawatts of capacity delivered or under development' on 'USD 5.9 billion' of committed equity and debt and 'USD 16.1 billion of planned investment' — figures its own website has since moved to 2.27+ GW and USD 7.4 billion — while the independently verifiable operating base is two buildings (Mesa PH01, 26 MW; Santa Clara SV01, 36 MW) and every tenant is unnamed.

BACKGROUND. Formed 14 February 2018 by Mount Elbert Capital Partners, GIC (lead anchor investor) and OPTrust with 'over US$800 million of equity' under founder-CEO Tom Ray (ex-CoreSite); sold to Partners Group on 11 November 2022 with a 476 MW portfolio across Phoenix, Reno, Santa Clara and Ashburn (price to the sellers undisclosed). Lee Kestler (ex-Vantage CCO, ex-DuPont Fabros) became CEO on 9 March 2023 and refocused the company in October 2023 on 'single tenant data centers' for hyperscalers and AI leaders under the 'Designed for Density' brand: 300+ MW campus designs, 36–144 MW buildings, rack densities 'well over 50 kW' with direct-to-chip liquid cooling readiness, and air-cooled closed-loop chilled water with water usage effectiveness 'below .01 L/kWh'. Six markets per the company: Mesa, AZ (496 MW, five buildings, SRP; Holder Construction as GC per third parties), Reno/Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center, NV (216 MW, three buildings, NV Energy), Santa Clara, CA (72 MW, two buildings, Silicon Valley Power), Sterling, VA (114 MW, two fully leased buildings, Dominion Energy, USD 1.5 billion of construction loans in April 2026), Culpeper, VA (196 MW, capacity from mid-2029, Rappahannock Electric Cooperative) and Louisa County, VA (the 'gigascale' Shannon Hill site: 1.1+ GW, 697 acres bought for USD 42 million, 'USD 17B+', by-right zoning). Capital is raised at project level as green limited-recourse term loans (USD 1.9 billion Mesa, USD 440 million Santa Clara, USD 1.1 billion Reno and Ashburn in 2024; USD 1.5 billion Sterling in 2026) plus a first USD 235 million ABS on the stabilized PH01 lease (July 2025). Collection gap: no tenant, no revenue, no headcount, no first-party GC and no ESG report; Partners Group's 2025 annual report mentions EdgeCore only as an illustrative label.
ecosystemRole: A sponsor-owned build-to-suit landlord for hyperscalers, and the source of the '1.8 GW delivered or under development on $16.1B planned' figure the coverage plan attached to the wrong row. EdgeCore is the developer-customer of Holder Construction on the Mesa and Santa Clara campuses, a Dominion Energy large-load customer at Sterling, an SRP customer whose Mesa expansion was redrawn around an SRP switchyard, and — with the August 2026 Ratepayer Protection Pledge — a self-declared 'pay for our own power delivery' developer. It competes for the same single-tenant hyperscale leases as Vantage, STACK, QTS, Aligned and Compass, and its executives are drawn from Vantage, QTS, STACK, DuPont Fabros, CoreSite and Digital Realty.

productsAndServices.name: Single-tenant hyperscale campuses — 'Designed for Density' (the core product)
productsAndServices.category: Wholesale data-center development, ownership and operation
productsAndServices.description: EdgeCore describes itself as 'a wholesale data center developer, owner and operator' offering 'both ready-for-occupancy and build-to-suit data center campuses that are designed for density'. Since the October 2023 repositioning it has 'concentrated exclusively on meeting the requirements of hyperscalers and leaders in the AI revolution'; Kestler in January 2026: 'Our focus is singular: build high-density, scalable, single tenant data centers with an absolute certainty of execution.' The campus standard is a '300+ MW design' with 'capacity of up to 1.2GW on a single campus'; buildings run '36-144 MW' (Data Center Frontier, 2023), with 'rack densities well over 50 kW' and designs that 'accommodate direct-to-chip liquid cooling'. Every campus page states a 'one building, one customer' model; the company says it 'has never missed a customer milestone' and met '10 out of 10' 2025 targets.
highlights: Portfolio per the six campus pages (September 2026): Mesa 496 MW critical IT load / 5 data centers / 84 acres; Reno 216 MW / 3 / 56 acres; Silicon Valley 72 MW / 2 / 12 acres; Ashburn (Sterling) 114 MW / 2 / 17 acres; Culpeper 196 MW / 2 / 93 acres; Louisa 1,100+ MW / 6 / 697 acres — a sum of about 2.19 GW, consistent with the homepage's '2.27+ GW'.

January 2026 milestone release: 'more than 1.8 gigawatts of capacity delivered or under development across its U.S. platform'; 'committed more than $5.9 billion in equity capital and debt'; 'backed by $16.1 billion of planned investment'; '7 million sq. ft.'; peak construction workforce 'more than 3500 skilled tradespeople'; '9M+' manhours.

Delivered and leased buildings that third parties can verify: PH01 Mesa ('26 MW IT capacity, fully leased to single hyperscale tenant', securitized July 2025) and SV01 Santa Clara (36 MW; ribbon-cutting 10 September 2025 with Holder Construction's president present). AS01/AS02 Sterling are 'fully leased' with occupancy targeted November 2026 and July 2027; PH02 (868,000 sq ft) topped out December 2024; Reno's first of three 72 MW buildings is under construction.

Contract form per Partners Group's investment case: 'The Company signs long-term contracts with large Tier 1 data center users'; 'customers charged a price based on their contracted power capacity, leading to highly visible cashflows'. EdgeCore publishes no lease term, rent or tenant name; Virginia Business (April 2026): the company 'declined to identify tenants or provide projected total construction cost'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Six self-stated differentiators: 'Prepared for Growth' (300+ MW campus design), 'Near-term Availability', 'Industry Experience', 'Pragmatic Designs', 'Timely Delivery', 'Layers of Security'. The claim that a hyperscale building 'typically requires 36+ months from groundbreaking to activation' is the yardstick EdgeCore says it beats through pre-permitted sites, secured power and repeatable designs. Named competitors: none on any first-party page; the executive bench comes from Vantage (Kestler, Conner, Thompson), QTS (Heiden), STACK (Thissen), DuPont Fabros, CoreSite and Digital Realty, which is the peer set in practice. The Culpeper site sits 0.52 miles from STACK's NVA10 (datacenterHawk).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct long-term leases to hyperscalers ('capacity@edgecore.com'); no broker or JV channel is described. Leased buildings are then financed with limited-recourse green loans and, once stabilized, securitized.
targetSegments: 'the world's largest cloud and internet companies' (boilerplate)
Hyperscalers and 'leaders in the AI revolution' taking whole buildings
Large-scale AI deployments requiring direct-to-chip liquid cooling
productsAndServices.roadmap: AS01 occupancy November 2026 and AS02 July 2027 (April 2026 release); Reno completion 'as early as 2026' with three 72 MW buildings; PH02/PH03 completions '2025 and 2026'; Culpeper 'capacity available beginning in mid 2029' (scaled down from 216/432 MW and an early-2028 target in the 2024 announcement); Louisa construction start not announced, water infrastructure by mid-2026 per local reporting; 'plans to expand into new regions in 2026 and beyond' with no site named.

productsAndServices.name: Gigascale campuses and powered-land pre-positioning (Louisa County, Mesa expansion)
productsAndServices.description: EdgeCore's 'Gigascale' page defines the product as '1+ gigawatt (1,000+ megawatts) of total power capacity' on 'pre-permitted sites, secured gigawatt power allocations, and repeatable designs'. Kestler (April 2026): 'EdgeCore deploys equity capital to preposition large land parcels, energy delivery assets and construction labor resources where we anticipate strong customer demand.' The flagship is the Shannon Hill Regional Business Park in Louisa County, Virginia — '1.1+ GW critical IT load', '697 acres' bought from the county's industrial development authority for 'USD 42 million' (about USD 60,000 an acre per local reporting), by-right zoning from a 2019 rezoning, 'USD 17B+' of planned investment, power from Rappahannock Electric Cooperative 'and affiliate Hyperscale Energy'.
highlights: Louisa: six data centers; '3.1M' sq ft on the homepage and location page against '3.9+ million' on the gigascale page and the June 2025 release — unreconciled; 'No state incentives provided for this project' (Virginia Business); a county supervisor speculated in June 2026 that EdgeCore might bring 'smaller gas plants or something, maybe small modular reactors' — EdgeCore did not respond.

Mesa expansion: 43.87 acres bought in May 2025 for USD 43.95 million from a Brookfield Properties affiliate, taking the campus to '450+ MW'; the expansion plan was cut in March 2026 from 2.1 million sq ft and three buildings to 1,236,960 sq ft and two buildings to accommodate an SRP switchyard expansion.

Culpeper: 120 acres in the Culpeper Technology Zone bought July 2024 (the campus page now shows 93 acres); 'not yet been commissioned or leased' and no on-site substation (datacenterHawk); regional opposition to the seven-campus Technology Zone and the Valley Link 765 kV line does not name EdgeCore.

Dropped and slipped sites: a Richardson/Dallas campus planned in 2018 ('up to 165 MW') disappears from every post-2022 portfolio list; Reno moved from a 136-acre, 400+ MW airport-adjacent site (August 2023 release) to a 56-acre, 216 MW site at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center without explanation, and its first building was still under construction in January 2026 against a 'late 2025' target.
productsAndServices.positioning: Pre-positioned land with secured utility allocations is EdgeCore's answer to the 36-month build cycle; the risk is that 'delivered or under development' counts land-stage megawatts — the 1.8 GW figure only reconciles if Louisa's 1.1 GW and unleased Culpeper are included.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sites are held on the company's balance sheet with sponsor equity and leased building-by-building; no powered-land sales are recorded.
targetSegments: Hyperscale tenants seeking 1 GW+ single-campus programmes
Virginia and Southwest markets 60–85 miles from constrained hubs (Ashburn, Phoenix)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Louisa buildings planned 2028–2033 per directory listings (unverified); performance agreement approved by the county board on 1 December 2025 per search results (not fetched).

productsAndServices.name: Water-neutral, air-cooled design standard (closed-loop chilled water, WUE below 0.01 L/kWh)
productsAndServices.description: Every campus page repeats the same thermal claim: 'air-cooled designs that include ultra-efficient close-looped chilled water systems' with water usage effectiveness 'below .01 L/kWh'; Silicon Valley adds 'PUE <1.3' and 'generator-backed air cooling and adiabatic dry coolers'; DLR Group's project page for Mesa Building 1 states 'PUE <1.25', '68 highly efficient chilled water Computer Room Air Handlers per building' and a 'non-raised floor system'. Mesa is described as a 'LEED-designed, water-neutral campus', where water-neutral means restoring 'water volume equal to withdrawals into geographically relevant watersheds' through an SRP partnership 'expected to achieve water-neutral status on the Mesa campus through 2036' (USD 288,419 and USD 280,560 contributed). Ashburn buildings are 'structurally engineered to accommodate liquid to liquid loads, including NVIDIA VR racks', with 'mechanical galleries sized for variable water-to-air cooling ratios'.
highlights: Certifications: Green Globes for Existing Buildings (PH01, 2023); 'Designed to Earn ENERGY STAR' (PH02, PH03); 'LEED BD+C v4 Silver standards'; member of the Data Center Coalition and iMasons Climate Accord.
MIT Technology Review (May 2025) independently confirms the Reno design 'will rely on an "air-cooled closed-loop chiller" that doesn't require water evaporation for cooling'.

Third-party gap: no independent source describes deployed liquid cooling at any EdgeCore building; the 2023–2024 building spec was '30-40 kW per rack' (air-cooling range) and the 50 kW+ / direct-to-chip language is design intent.
No ESG or sustainability report exists on the site; PUE and WUE figures are unaudited design values.
productsAndServices.positioning: Water is the siting constraint in Arizona, Nevada and rural Virginia; a closed-loop, near-zero-WUE design is what lets EdgeCore build in Mesa and at TRIC, where regional water opposition (Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe, Basin and Range Watch) targets evaporative designs.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal design standard applied to every campus; not sold separately.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Liquid-to-liquid capability at Ashburn AS01/AS02 (occupancy from November 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Project-level green financing and sponsor equity
productsAndServices.description: EdgeCore finances each leased campus with limited-recourse senior secured term loans structured as green loans (ING as green-loan structuring agent in every deal), refinances stabilized leases through securitization, and takes equity from Partners Group's client programmes. 2024: 'USD 1.9 billion' for Mesa (MUFG administrative agent; TD Securities, ING, Scotiabank, Santander — 'the company's first green loan'), 'USD 1.1 billion' for Reno and Ashburn (MUFG), 'USD 440 million' for Santa Clara SV01 (MUFG, ING, First-Citizens; borrower MECP1 Santa Clara 1, LLC), and a 'USD 1.9 billion' equity investment led by Partners Group 'with multiple global co-investors' ('significant syndication from our clients' per Partners Group's 2024 annual report). 2025: 'USD 235 million' ABS backed by PH01 (MUFG structuring agent; Goldman Sachs, TD Securities; issuer ECore 2025-1; S&P A- and BBB- on the first two tranches per Commercial Property Executive). 2026: 'USD 1.5 billion' for Sterling AS01/AS02 (Apterra Infrastructure Capital, Global Infrastructure Partners/BlackRock, ING).
highlights: Cumulative company claims: 'USD 4.24 billion' across three 2024 transactions (the three named deals sum to USD 4.9 billion — the company's arithmetic is unexplained); 'more than $5.9 billion in equity capital and debt' (January 2026); '$7.4 billion' committed and '$16.1B' planned investment (site, September 2026).

Ownership chain: Partners Group acquired EdgeCore 'on behalf of its clients' (November 2022, up to USD 1.2 billion covering acquisition and buildout); Partners Group Holding AG is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (PGHN) but no source describes EdgeCore as a balance-sheet holding of the listed company; prior owners GIC, OPTrust and Mount Elbert are not named as sellers by either party.

Sponsor voice: Fentress Boyse (Partners Group, Infrastructure Americas) in the 2026 financing release; Nils Rode (Partners Group CIO) in the 2025 ABS release; Ed Diffendal in the 2022 and 2024 releases; the 2023 board adds operating directors Heather Dooley, Mark Sokol and Brian Mattson (ex-Google/Microsoft).

Rating context: EdgeCore's first ABS was rated by S&P alone (A-/BBB-), against the AAA Moody's gave Compass's February 2026 hyperscale ABS — the securitization market differentiates by collateral seasoning and agency.
productsAndServices.positioning: The structure keeps recourse at the campus: each borrower is a single-purpose entity (MECP1 Mesa 1 LLC, MECP1 Santa Clara 1 LLC) and the loans are sized to a signed hyperscale lease, which is why EdgeCore can announce 'fully leased' financings without naming the tenant.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bank syndicates (MUFG, ING, TD, Scotiabank, Santander, First-Citizens, Apterra, GIP) and Rule 144A ABS.
targetSegments: Partners Group client programmes and co-investors
productsAndServices.roadmap: '$16.1 billion of planned investment to fund the development of additional hyperscale and AI-ready data center campuses' (January 2026) — no dated drawdown schedule is published.

recentDevelopments.headline: Data Center Knowledge: 'EdgeCore Says Data Centers Should Pay Their Own Power Costs' — EVP Finance Julie Brewer: 'We expect to bear 100% of the costs' of power delivery infrastructure, 'roughly 5-10% of upfront project costs'; EdgeCore 'will abandon projects if power economics become financially unworkable'
recentDevelopments.read: The developer is pricing ratepayer politics into site selection and saying so — a walk-away threshold on power cost is unusual candour for a landlord.

recentDevelopments.headline: EdgeCore signs the Ratepayer Protection Pledge: 'Build/bring/buy new power supply; pay for new power delivery infrastructure; pay whether power is used or not; invest in local jobs and workforce development; contribute to grid and community resilience'
recentDevelopments.read: A voluntary federal pledge that mirrors the take-or-pay and infrastructure-funding terms utilities such as SRP and ComEd are already writing into large-load tariffs.

recentDevelopments.headline: AS02 Sterling tops out, following AS01 in September 2025; completion targeted July 2027
recentDevelopments.read: Northern Virginia delivery is on the schedule the April 2026 financing assumed.

recentDevelopments.headline: A Louisa County supervisor speculates that EdgeCore's Shannon Hill campus might bring 'smaller gas plants or something, maybe small modular reactors'; EdgeCore does not respond
recentDevelopments.read: Power sourcing for a 1.1 GW rural campus on a cooperative's system is the open question the company has not answered publicly.

recentDevelopments.headline: Greg Thompson appointed SVP, Enterprise Security (ex-CISO of VHC Health and Vantage Data Centers; ex-FBI) as EdgeCore 'establishes enterprise security function'
recentDevelopments.read: Another Vantage alumnus; the function is a hyperscaler procurement requirement rather than a growth signal.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 1.5 billion of construction financing for the two fully leased Sterling data centers (114 MW, 685,000 sq ft): two senior secured limited-recourse term loans from Apterra, Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) and ING; occupancy November 2026 and July 2027
recentDevelopments.read: GIP as a lender rather than an owner shows where the infrastructure funds sit in EdgeCore's stack; the release also restates '1.8 gigawatts' and '1.4 GWs under development in Northern and Central Virginia'.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mesa Planning & Zoning approves a revised expansion: 1,236,960 sq ft in two buildings, down from 2.1 million sq ft and three, 'to accommodate an SRP switchyard expansion'; the 43.87 acres were bought in May 2025 for USD 43.95 million from a Brookfield Properties affiliate
recentDevelopments.read: The utility's need for switchyard land cost EdgeCore roughly 800,000 sq ft of building — a concrete example of power infrastructure setting the campus footprint.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'EdgeCore Enters 2026 with 1.8GW of Data Center Capacity Delivered or Under Development': USD 5.9 billion committed, USD 16.1 billion planned, 7 million sq ft, 10 of 10 customer milestones met, 145% employee growth, 3,500+ peak trades
recentDevelopments.read: The headline figure counts planning-stage Louisa; the independently verifiable operating base is two buildings. The clause the coverage plan attached to Compass belongs here.

recentDevelopments.headline: Interglobix reports the 10 September 2025 ribbon-cutting of SV01 in Santa Clara with Mayor Lisa Gillmor and Holder Construction president Beth Lowry
recentDevelopments.read: The second delivered building — land bought in 2018, ground broken January 2023, opened September 2025: a 32-month build on a 12-acre urban site.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 235 million ABS backed by PH01 Mesa (26 MW, fully leased to a single hyperscale tenant): MUFG structuring agent, Goldman Sachs and TD Securities; Partners Group CIO Nils Rode quoted; S&P A- and BBB- on the first two tranches (Commercial Property Executive)
recentDevelopments.read: EdgeCore's entry into the data-center ABS market on one stabilized lease — a proof of concept for refinancing Mesa and Sterling once occupied.

recentDevelopments.headline: Louisa County, Virginia: 'USD 17B+' gigascale campus — 1.1+ GW, 697 acres bought from the county IDA for USD 42 million, six buildings, Rappahannock Electric Cooperative and Hyperscale Energy; Governor Youngkin quoted; no state incentives
recentDevelopments.read: The single largest addition to the portfolio (roughly half of today's 2.27 GW) is a land-and-power position 85 miles from Ashburn with no announced tenant or construction date.

recentDevelopments.headline: Steve Conner appointed President (ex-Vantage CTO and SVP Solution and Architecture Engineering); team up 80% since February 2025
recentDevelopments.read: A second ex-Vantage executive in the top two seats; the company is staffing for a multi-campus construction programme.

recentDevelopments.headline: Metro Phoenix market expanded to '450+ MW' with 43.87 additional acres; SRP CEO Jim Pratt quoted; PH01 Green Globes, PH02/PH03 'Designed to Earn ENERGY STAR'
recentDevelopments.read: Mesa is the anchor market: three buildings built or building and another 250+ MW planned on land bought from Brookfield Properties.

recentDevelopments.headline: Personnel expansion: Ruben Thissen (SVP Operations and EHS, founding STACK executive, ex-Microsoft), Therese Kerfoot promoted to EVP Strategy, Bill Jabjiniak to SVP community and government relations
recentDevelopments.read: The hires map the model — operations from a hyperscaler, strategy from CoreSite, community relations from the City of Mesa's former economic-development director.

recentDevelopments.headline: PH02 (868,000 sq ft) tops out in Mesa with general contractor Holder Construction; Arizona Corporation Commissioner Kevin Thompson attends
recentDevelopments.read: The only public naming of a GC on an EdgeCore campus comes from the GC and the trade press, never from EdgeCore.

recentDevelopments.headline: Partners Group completes a USD 1.9 billion equity investment in EdgeCore with multiple global co-investors, remaining majority investor; EdgeCore counts USD 4.24 billion across three 2024 transactions
recentDevelopments.read: Sponsor equity syndicated to Partners Group's clients funds the land bank ahead of leases; the company's USD 4.24 billion total does not match the three named deals (USD 4.9 billion).

recentDevelopments.headline: New market: Culpeper, Virginia — 120 acres in the Culpeper Technology Zone, '216MW' initial and 'up to 432MW', power from Rappahannock Electric Cooperative as early as 2028
recentDevelopments.read: Announced at twice the capacity and 18 months earlier than the campus page now shows (196 MW, mid-2029) — the clearest documented scale-down in the portfolio.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 440 million green loan for Santa Clara SV01 (36 MW) from MUFG, ING and First-Citizens — Data Center Frontier records the 2024 building spec: 36 MW minimum per building, three data halls, at least two storeys, 30–40 kW per rack
recentDevelopments.read: The 2024 spec is an air-cooled, 30–40 kW design; the '50 kW+ / direct-to-chip' language postdates it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Second 2024 debt financing: USD 1.1 billion for the Reno and Ashburn campuses (MUFG administrative agent), taking 2024 debt to USD 3.0 billion
recentDevelopments.read: Every campus is financed separately against its own lease — the limited-recourse pattern that lets an unnamed-tenant developer borrow at scale.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 1.9 billion senior secured credit facility for the flagship Mesa campus (MUFG, TD Securities, ING, Scotiabank, Santander; borrower MECP1 Mesa 1, LLC) — 'the company's first green loan'
recentDevelopments.read: The figure that Construction Dive's headline later styled as a 'USD 1.9B ... job' for Holder — it is EdgeCore's debt, not a contract value.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Designed for Density' repositioning: 300+ MW campuses, USD 600 million planned for new regions in 2024; Kestler: 'The new EdgeCore is born in the age of AI'
recentDevelopments.read: The pivot from a 'land and expand' enterprise-and-cloud developer (2018) to a hyperscale-only single-tenant builder.

recentDevelopments.headline: Lee Kestler appointed CEO, succeeding Lex Coors (CEO since the November 2022 acquisition); Kestler had joined in 2019 as President and COO and chaired the board after Partners Group's investment
recentDevelopments.read: The sponsor put its board chair in the CEO seat four months after closing — the operating reset that preceded the AI repositioning.

recentDevelopments.headline: EdgeCore 'has re-capitalized and is now owned by Partners Group, a leading global private market firm acting on behalf of its clients'; initial commitment 'up to USD 1.2 billion' for existing and under-construction sites and future buildout
recentDevelopments.read: Ownership passed from GIC, OPTrust and Mount Elbert to a Swiss-listed manager's client funds; the price to the sellers was never disclosed.

relationships.note: General contractor on the Mesa campus (PH02, PH03) and Santa Clara SV01 — named by Holder, the trade press and the City of Mesa, never by EdgeCore.
relationships.context:
AZ Big Media's December 2024 topping-out coverage names Holder Construction as general contractor for PH02 (868,000 sq ft); Proximo lists Holder as EPC contractor on PH03; Mesa's January 2024 planning record states 'the general contractor is Holder Construction'; and Holder's president Beth Lowry attended the September 2025 SV01 ribbon-cutting in Santa Clara, where the structural-frame vendor's project page also lists Holder as GC. Construction Dive's January 2024 headline 'Holder Construction gets $1.9B Arizona data center job' refers to EdgeCore's USD 1.9 billion debt financing; the article states no contract value.

Not supported: any Holder role at Sterling, Reno, Culpeper or Louisa — no GC is named for those sites in any fetched source.
relationships.via: Mesa PH02/PH03 and Santa Clara SV01

relationships.note: Power provider for the Sterling AS01/AS02 campus (114 MW), per the April 2026 financing coverage.

policyExposure.regime: Arizona Computer Data Center Program (tax-exemption pause)
policyExposure.exposure: Laws 2026 Ch. 140 (HB 4168), signed 13 June 2026, bars the Arizona Commerce Authority from accepting new Computer Data Center Program applications from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2029; 113 applications were filed in the last two weeks of June. EdgeCore's Mesa expansion (250+ MW planned) is the exposure; whether its buildings hold grandfathered certifications is not disclosed.

Laws 2026 Ch. 111 lets the Arizona Corporation Commission set 'minimum bills, contract terms, infrastructure-payment requirements, and collateral provisions' for 'extra high load factor customers' and requires utilities to report interconnection requests semi-annually. SRP's 2025 Large Customer Integration Process already requires customers to fund dedicated upgrades upfront, and SRP's switchyard needs forced EdgeCore to cut its Mesa expansion by a building in March 2026.
policyExposure.mitigation: EdgeCore's stated posture (Brewer, August 2026): 'We expect to bear 100% of the costs' of power delivery infrastructure, and the company signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge on 13 August 2026.

policyExposure.exposure: A voluntary federal pledge (launched March 2026, expanded July 2026 per Data Center Knowledge) that EdgeCore signed on 13 August 2026: build, bring or buy new power supply; pay for new power delivery infrastructure; pay whether power is used or not; invest in local jobs; contribute to grid and community resilience. It does not determine utility cost allocation.

policyExposure.regime: Virginia data-center sales-and-use tax exemption and electricity consumption tax
policyExposure.exposure: The 2026 Virginia budget preserved the long-standing sales and use tax exemption for qualifying data-center equipment but added an electricity consumption tax of USD 0.011 per kWh from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028, capped at USD 600 million a year, with a tax-policy study due 15 December 2026. Exposure: three Virginia campuses (Sterling 114 MW, Culpeper 196 MW, Louisa 1.1+ GW). Louisa received no state incentives; Culpeper County has no computer-equipment tax.

Mesa's July 2025 ordinance confines data centers to general/heavy industrial districts with a council-approved PAD overlay; EdgeCore's Elliot Road expansion 'predates those regulations' and was re-approved by Planning & Zoning in March 2026 without neighbour objection.

periods.commentary: Collection gap: the listed sponsor discloses nothing usable about EdgeCore; the only priced facts are the loans, the ABS and two land purchases. No 'expected' benchmarks exist for a private developer and none are manufactured.

financials.commentary: A private, sponsor-owned developer whose every disclosed number is a financing or a land deal. Size it from the pieces: up to USD 1.2 billion committed at the 2022 acquisition (price to sellers undisclosed), USD 1.9 billion of syndicated sponsor equity in 2024, about USD 5.2 billion of announced campus-level debt since 2024, and a company-stated USD 7.4 billion committed against USD 16.1 billion 'planned'. The independently verifiable operating base is two buildings (PH01 26 MW; SV01 36 MW); everything else is under construction or land.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that EdgeCore's '1.8 GW delivered or under development' (January 2026) and '2.27+ GW' (site) are land-and-pipeline counts, not delivered capacity, and that the verifiable operating base is about 62 MW in two buildings. Basis: PH01 (26 MW, securitized) and SV01 (36 MW, opened September 2025) are the only buildings third parties record as operating; Sterling's two buildings are financed and topped out but occupy from November 2026; Reno's first building was still under construction in January 2026; Culpeper is 'not yet been commissioned or leased'; and the portfolio figure only reconciles if Louisa's planning-stage 1.1 GW is counted. 'Under development' is doing most of the work in the headline.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the company's operating model is the sponsor-financed single-tenant build-to-suit, executed at project level: pre-positioned land and utility allocations funded by Partners Group's client equity, a signed hyperscale lease, then a limited-recourse green loan sized to that lease and, once stabilized, an ABS. Basis: four campus loans (USD 1.9 billion, 1.1 billion, 440 million, 1.5 billion) each tied to named buildings and unnamed tenants; the ECore 2025-1 ABS on one lease; Partners Group's investment thesis ('customers charged a price based on their contracted power capacity'); and Kestler's 'preposition large land parcels, energy delivery assets and construction labor resources' statement. The tenant's identity is the one variable the whole structure is built to keep private.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Louisa County is the bet that decides EdgeCore's next five years, and that its power supply is unresolved. Basis: 697 acres and 1.1+ GW represent roughly half of the stated portfolio and 'USD 17B+' of planned investment on a cooperative's system (Rappahannock Electric Cooperative and 'affiliate Hyperscale Energy') 85 miles from Ashburn, with no announced tenant, GC, construction date or generation plan; a county supervisor's June 2026 speculation about gas plants or SMRs drew no company response; and the regional Valley Link 765 kV line faces organised opposition. A named tenant or a filed generation or transmission plan would move this judgment either way.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that schedule risk in the portfolio is higher than the '100% Customer Milestones Met' claim implies, because the milestones are set after leases are signed while the campuses slip before them. Basis: Reno was a 2018 launch market that broke ground in 2023 and moved sites without explanation; Richardson/Dallas (165 MW, 2018) disappeared from every later list; Culpeper was announced at 216/432 MW with power in early 2028 and now shows 196 MW from mid-2029; Mesa's expansion lost a building to an SRP switchyard in 2026. The claim is true for leased buildings and silent about the pipeline.

5. **(High confidence)** We assess that EdgeCore has chosen to lead on the ratepayer question rather than resist it: 'We expect to bear 100% of the costs' of power delivery, the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, self-funded substations at every campus and a stated willingness to 'abandon projects if power economics become financially unworkable'. Basis: the August 2026 Data Center Knowledge interview and pledge release, SRP's Large Customer Integration Process, Arizona's HB 2756 and the ICC/ComEd-style deposit rules spreading across its markets. The posture converts an external constraint into a marketing claim, at the price of a walk-away threshold the company has now stated publicly.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess that liquid cooling at EdgeCore is design readiness rather than deployed capability. Basis: the 2023–2024 building specification was 30–40 kW per rack air cooling; the 'well over 50 kW' and 'direct-to-chip' language appears on 2026 pages and the Ashburn campus is described as 'engineered to accommodate' liquid-to-liquid loads; no third-party source describes an operating liquid-cooled EdgeCore hall. A named liquid-cooled deployment (AS01, November 2026) would settle this.

Collection gap: no tenant at any campus; no revenue, EBITDA, headcount or valuation; no first-party GC; no ESG report; the sellers in the 2022 deal and the price paid are undisclosed; the 'USD 4.24 billion' 2024 total and the 3.1M/3.9M sq ft Louisa figures are the company's own unreconciled numbers; Data Center Dynamics (the outlet most likely to have named tenants) was unreadable. Premise check against the coverage-plan row 'Brookfield-owned hyperscale builder; 1.8 GW delivered or under development on $16.1B planned; Joliet 1.8 GW campus': only the middle clause describes EdgeCore, and it is EdgeCore's own January 2026 wording — true as stated then, already superseded by the site's 2.27+ GW and USD 7.4 billion; EdgeCore is Partners Group-owned (its only Brookfield link is the purchase of Mesa land from a Brookfield Properties affiliate) and has no Illinois site.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *November 2026 — AS01 occupancy in Sterling:* on time would be the first delivery under the 2023 repositioning and the first liquid-ready hall; a slip would undercut the milestone claim. *2026 — Reno RN01 energisation and NV Energy power delivery:* the campus is a year past its late-2025 target. *Any Louisa County filing naming a tenant, a generation source or a construction start:* the trigger for Judgment 3. *A second ABS or a refinancing of the Mesa USD 1.9 billion facility:* would show whether the 2025 A-/BBB- ratings improve with seasoning, against Compass's Moody's AAA. *Arizona Corporation Commission rules under HB 2756 and the 2029 exemption sunset:* would price the Mesa expansion. *A Partners Group exit process (sale, continuation vehicle or IPO):* Partners Group's client programmes are finite-life funds; four years in, an exit path is the structural question.
